export_controls.text:
Trump asked oil and gas CEOs to chip in $1BN to his campaign - they did - and they keep getting results. The corruption is sickening, never-ending and devastating for our health and safety.

Ignoring the climate and AI crises will only hurt us. https://t.co/yKiKQyFvED

deepseek.reason: The statement discusses campaign corruption and climate/AI crises, not export controls.
deepseek.confidence_reason: No mention of export controls or overseas AI access.

china_race_dynamics.text: 68,000 people exposed. Hackers with an open-source AI tool. No country can fight this alone. The U.S. and China must cooperate on AI security now, before our financial system is next. https://t.co/JZfKqnPSn7

deepseek.reason: The speaker calls for U.S.-China cooperation on AI security but does not explicitly endorse or reject competition as a policy priority.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The cooperation facet is explicit, but the stance on competition priority is ambiguous because cooperation and competition can coexist.

astra.reason: She demands US–China AI security cooperation without saying whether competition should remain a policy priority.
astra.confidence_reason: The cooperation endorsement is clear, while the direction on competitive prioritization remains unstated.

china_race_dynamics.text:
This is an unacceptable position from President Trump and will end in catastrophe. 

It is the government’s job to regulate industry — especially frontier AI that has the capacity to harm human beings at a massive scale. 

I urge President Trump to take this threat seriously and take real action. It’s also imperative the U.S. lead negotiations with China to develop global rules of the road on AI.

deepseek.reason: The speaker urges U.S. negotiations with China on global AI rules, without stating a position on making competition a priority.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The statement advocates cooperation but does not address competition priority.

astra.reason: She urges negotiations with China on global AI rules without specifying a position on prioritizing competition.
astra.confidence_reason: Negotiations are explicitly endorsed, but neither a competitive priority nor a competitive safety tradeoff is stated.

china_race_dynamics.text: Frontier AI isn't going to care if you're American or if you're Chinese or if you're Russian. This highly capable, advanced technology could be a threat to all humans. That's why I'm calling on President Trump to work with countries like China to set global rules on the development of Frontier AI.

deepseek.reason: The speaker urges working with China on global rules for frontier AI, without addressing whether competition should be a priority.
deepseek.confidence_reason: Cooperation is clear, but competition priority is not discussed.

astra.reason: She advocates global frontier AI rules with China without explicitly rejecting or endorsing competition as a priority.
astra.confidence_reason: The shared-threat framing supports cooperation but does not explicitly reject a competitive approach.

china_race_dynamics.text: I'm leading dozens of my colleagues in demanding the Trump Administration take urgent action to address highly capable frontier AI - immediately. We need to work with our international partners and also our competitors, like China, to avert potentially devastating consequences. https://t.co/JCZN6eMiwz

deepseek.reason: The speaker calls for working with competitors like China to avert AI consequences, but does not state whether competition should be a policy priority.
deepseek.confidence_reason: Cooperation is explicit, but the stance on competition priority is not stated.

astra.reason: She calls for cooperation with China on frontier AI risks without stating whether competition should be a policy priority.
astra.confidence_reason: Cooperation is explicit, but its implications for prioritizing competition are unstated.

china_race_dynamics.text:
Maybe we should listen to our constituents and do something about it then!! 

We need to immediately pause the development of frontier AI. Then we need public, bipartisan hearings in Congress, meaningful regulations, a new federal agency charged with oversight of AI, and an international treaty with China as well as our allies to set global rules to prevent an AI arms race.

deepseek.reason: The speaker calls for an international treaty with China to prevent an AI arms race and to pause frontier AI development.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The statement explicitly rejects an AI arms race and urges a pause and treaty.

china_race_dynamics.text: We strongly urge your administration to lead a coordinated international effort to establish a global framework to guide the development of this technology and a shared vision for AI end-use — engaging our strongest allies, such as the European Union, as well as formidable global competitors, particularly the People’s Republic of China.

deepseek.reason: The speaker urges international cooperation and mentions China as a competitor but does not endorse making competition with China a policy priority.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The cooperation facet is explicit, but the stance on race priority is inferential because the statement does not directly endorse or reject it.

astra.reason: The speaker urges AI cooperation with China without endorsing or rejecting competition with China as a policy priority.
astra.confidence_reason: Cooperation is explicit, but the statement takes no position on prioritizing competition.

china_race_dynamics.text:
It’s urgent that Democrats and Republicans in Congress unite to pass meaningful regulations on AI. When the engineers and CEOs building this rapidly accelerating technology are warning us of its existential threat to humanity, it would be deeply irresponsible to ignore their expertise.

Just as we regulate pharmaceutical drugs, nuclear weapons, airplanes and so much more, we must regulate frontier AI before there are catastrophic consequences.

Further, the U.S. must lead negotiations with China to establish a global framework on this issue. Donald Trump has an opportunity to do tremendous good here. Again—we’ve done it before and we can do it again. International cooperation is in all of our best interests.

deepseek.reason: The speaker calls for U.S. negotiations with China and international cooperation rather than making competition the priority.
deepseek.confidence_reason: Clear cooperation call, though it does not explicitly discuss race priority.

china_race_dynamics.text: Uncontrollable, highly capable frontier AI is a threat to all of us. It doesn’t matter if you’re a Democrat or Republican, American or Chinese. We need to set global AI rules, full stop. https://t.co/xJDOc6eNHk

deepseek.reason: The speaker says the threat is shared by Americans and Chinese and calls for global AI rules, rejecting a competition-first framing.
deepseek.confidence_reason: Explicit cooperation language, but no direct mention of competition priority to reject.

astra.reason: The speaker advocates global rules for shared American and Chinese AI risks without endorsing or rejecting competition with China.
astra.confidence_reason: Global rule-setting clearly favors cooperation, but the connection to competitive policy priorities is indirect.

No. This can’t be it. 

We need federal regulation, guardrails, and global coordination urgently. The President could lead diplomatic efforts to reach a global AI framework — one that ensures we maintain our national security as well as our collective safety. https://t.co/3nVdxNMPGw
